cases.name: randomIntercept_balanced
cases.note: Eight groups of six, random intercept only. The simplest case that has a variance component to get wrong.

cases.name: randomIntercept_unbalanced
cases.note: Unequal group sizes, which is where a method-of-moments start and a likelihood optimum diverge most.

cases.name: randomIntercept_smallVariance
cases.note: A random-effect variance far below the residual variance, where an estimator that floors it at zero would still look plausible.

cases.name: randomSlope_balanced
cases.note: Random intercept and slope, r = 2. The G matrix now has an off-diagonal the diagonal-only checks in the suite cannot see.

cases.name: randomSlope_unbalanced
cases.note: Random slope with unequal group sizes and more groups.

cases.name: randomIntercept_manyGroups
cases.note: Forty small groups — the regime where REML and ML differ most, so an implementation quietly computing ML would show here.

name: mixedModels
note: Generated once by Scripts/reference-fixtures/generate_mixed_models.py. The data is recorded alongside the estimates because both sides must fit the same problem. The REML log-likelihood is deliberately absent: implementations differ by additive constants in it, so two correct fits can disagree. Beta, G and the residual variance carry no such convention.
